review_candidates.title: Personal Assistant
review_candidates.description: Position Summary: The Executive Affairs Officer is responsible for providing comprehensive administrative, personal, family, household, travel, property, and financial coordination support to the CEO/President and his family.   The position serves as a trusted and highly organized point person for the day-to-day management and coordination of the family’s personal affairs, schedules, travel arrangements, household requirements, family activities, properties, vehicles, household staff, payments, and other personal administrative matters. The role requires a high level of confidentiality, discretion, integrity, initiative, attention to detail, and reliability, as the position will have access to sensitive personal, financial, family, and business-related information.   KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: A.  Executive and Personal Assistance Manage and coordinate the CEO/President’s personal schedule, appointments, commitments, and activities. Handle personal errands and administrative requests of the CEO/President. Coordinate personal appointments, reservations, meetings, and engagements. Assist in organizing personal-related travel requirements. Anticipate the CEO/President’s personal needs and proactively coordinate necessary arrangements. Maintain organized records of personal schedules, commitments, documents, and important dates. Handle sensitive and confidential information with utmost discretion. B.  Travel and Transportation Management Arrange domestic and international travel plans, including: Airline bookings Hotel accommodations Ground transportation Airport transfers Visa requirements Travel insurance Itineraries Restaurant and activity reservations, when required Prepare comprehensive travel itineraries and supporting documents. Coordinate changes, cancellations, rebooking, and other travel-related concerns. Coordinate transportation requirements for the CEO, family members, and guests. Ensure drivers are properly scheduled for airport transfers, personal appointments, school activities, and other commitments. C.  Family and Children’s Affairs Manage and coordinate schedules and appointments of family members and children. Coordinate children’s school activities, appointments, events, extracurricular activities, and other commitments. Monitor school-related requirements, payments, activities, and deadlines. Coordinate transportation and driver requirements for children’s activities. Assist in arranging supplies, materials, uniforms, activities, and other family requirements. Maintain an updated family calendar to ensure all schedules and commitments are properly coordinated. D.  Household Administration Coordinate the day-to-day administrative requirements of the household. Manage grocery, market, household supplies, and other household purchases. Monitor household inventory and ensure essential supplies are replenished on time. Coordinate payment of household utilities, bills, subscriptions, and other recurring expenses. Maintain proper records of household expenses and payments. Manage household petty cash and ensure proper documentation of all disbursements. Coordinate household repairs, maintenance, service providers, and other requirements. E.  Household Staff Administration Prepare and maintain payslips and payment records for household helpers. Coordinate monthly government remittances and related compliance requirements for household staff, including SSS, Pag-IBIG, and PhilHealth. Maintain accurate records of household staff schedules, compensation, benefits, and other administrative matters. Coordinate day-to-day operations of Kasambahays and Yayas Coordinate schedules, assignments, overtime, official business, and other requirements of household drivers. Monitor and manage driver-related petty cash and expense documentation. Coordinate with household staff to ensure assigned responsibilities and schedules are properly carried out. F. Property and Maintenance Management Monitor the maintenance schedules of the residence and other family properties. Coordinate preventive maintenance and servicing of: Air-conditioning units Pest control Plumbing and electrical requirements Appliances Other household equipment and facilities Maintain a calendar of recurring maintenance requirements. Coordinate with contractors, suppliers, technicians, and service providers. Monitor annual property dues, association dues, real property taxes/amilyar, and other property-related obligations. Maintain organized records of property-related payments and documents. G.  Vehicle Administration Monitor vehicle registration renewal schedules. Coordinate vehicle insurance renewal and related requirements. Maintain records of vehicle documents, insurance policies, registration, and other important information. Coordinate preventive maintenance and servicing schedules, when required. Coordinate with drivers regarding vehicle-related requirements and documentation. Ensure that renewal deadlines and vehicle-related obligations are monitored and completed on time. H.  Financial and Expense Administration Maintain and monitor petty cash for household and personal expenses. Record, organize, and reconcile household-related expenses. Summarize and monitor personal and family credit card expenses. Prepare periodic expense summaries for the CEO/President’s review. Coordinate payment of personal, household, property, vehicle, and family-related expenses. Maintain proper supporting documents and receipts for all expenses. Monitor recurring payments and ensure that no important payment or renewal deadline is missed. Coordinate with accounting, banks, financial institutions, or authorized representatives when required. Assist in monitoring investments and maintaining organized records of investment-related information, transactions, and schedules, as authorized by the CEO/President. I.  Family Office and Administrative Coordination Maintain an organized master calendar covering the CEO/President, spouse, children, household, drivers, properties, travel, and important deadlines. Maintain a centralized tracker for: Bills and payments Insurance renewals Vehicle registration Property dues and taxes School payments Household staff requirements Maintenance schedules Travel arrangements Important family dates Coordinate with external service providers, schools, banks, insurance companies, government agencies, property administrators, and other relevant parties. Follow up on pending personal and family-related matters until completion. Provide regular status updates to the CEO/President.   J.  Confidentiality, Security and Professional Conduct Maintain strict confidentiality over all personal, family, financial, business, travel, and household information. Exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive documents, conversations, transactions, and requests. Do not disclose personal or family information to unauthorized individuals. Maintain professional boundaries and appropriate conduct when dealing with household staff, suppliers, service providers, and third parties. Protect documents, keys, access information, personal records, and other sensitive materials entrusted to the position. Immediately report unusual, sensitive, or potentially significant concerns to the CEO/President. QUALIFICATIONS Educational Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Management, Office Administration, Hospitality Management, Accounting, Finance, or a related field preferred. Candidates with relevant extensive experience in executive assistance, private household management, family office administration, or personal affairs management may also be considered. Experience At least 3–5 years of experience in any of the following: Personal Assistant Executive Secretary Family Office Assistant Private Office Assistant Household/Family Affairs Manager Administrative Officer Executive Concierge Similar high-trust administrative role Experience working directly with executives, business owners, principals, or high-level families is highly preferred. Experience handling travel arrangements, household administration, financial documentation, or family schedules is an advantage. Technical Competencies Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint. Proficient in using Google Workspace and calendar management tools. Strong ability to maintain trackers, schedules, expense records, and administrative databases. Basic understanding of household financial management and expense reconciliation. Familiarity with government remittance processes such as SSS, Pag-IBIG, and PhilHealth is an advantage. Strong documentation and record-keeping skills. Comfortable coordinating online bookings, travel platforms, payment systems, and service providers. AI-literacy is a great advantage Preferred Additional Qualifications From South - Laguna (Verdana) and Cavite (Vista Verde) A valid driver’s license is an advantage. Willingness to travel when required. Willingness to work at the CEO/President’s residence/private office. Experience working with private families or high-net-worth individuals is an advantage. A strong network of reliable suppliers and service providers is an advantage. Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.  Can work Monday to Friday, and as needed during weekends. Core Competencies Highly Trustworthy and Discreet Highly Organized Detail-Oriented Proactive and Anticipatory Excellent Follow-Through Strong Communication Skills Resourceful and Problem-Solving Financially Responsible Flexible and Service-Oriented Mature and Professional

Vos tâches principales Les projets qui seront pilotés par la personne engagée sont : 1- Panneaux photovoltaïques – déploiement, optimisation et entretien-maintenance : Gérer l’ambitieux programme de déploiement de panneaux photovoltaiques sur les toitures communales ; Optimiser les systèmes de partage d’énergie pair-à-pair implémentés entre bâtiments communaux ; 2- Rénovation Et Isolation Des Toitures Lancer des études de stabilité de certaines toitures communales et analyser les résultats ; Préparer et gérer les projets de renforcement structurel, de rénovation et d’isolation des toitures, en prévision de la pose de panneaux photovoltaïques. 3- Nouvelles technologies, réseau d’énergie thermique, géothermie et riothermie : Etudier le potentiel de nouvelles technologies d’énergie renouvelable, concrètement, pour certains bâtiments spécifiques de la commune ; Proposer et lancer des projets pour déployer ces nouvelles technologies. Au quotidien les activités sont très variées : Vous évaluez la faisabilité des projets sur les plans technique, économique et humain ; Vous programmez et pilotez les différentes phases des projets ; Vous établissez les dossiers d’exécution (cahiers de charges, métrés, …) ; Vous participez à la passation des marchés publics (en collaboration avec la cellule Achat) ; Vous gérez les plannings, pilotez les partenaires, assurez l’exécution des marchés et assurez le suivi administratif et financier des projets ainsi que la gestion des marchés publics qui y contribuent ; Vous participez aux réunions de chantier et aux réceptions techniques, provisoires et définitives ; Vous analysez, évaluez et présentez les résultats à la hiérarchie (gains énergétiques par rapport aux estimations, capitalisation et propositions d’amélioration). Profil Vous disposez d’un diplôme de Master spécialisé en « énergie », « électricité », ou « construction » avec une appétence particulière pour les sujets énergétiques (une équivalence belge est exigée pour les diplômes obtenus à l’étranger) ; Une première expérience professionnelle en gestion de projets et/ou en matière de projets « toitures » et/ou « énergie renouvelable » est un atout ; Vous êtes à l’écoute et ouvert-e d’esprit, néanmoins vous faites preuve de conviction et savez fédérer des agents pour la réussite de vos projets ; Pragmatique et orienté·e terrain, vous recherchez un emploi qui allie théorie et pratique ; Une connaissance de base de la réglementation sur les marchés publics constitue un atout ; Vous êtes « orienté·e solutions » et autonome, capable de gérer votre temps, de fixer les priorités et de planifier les actions à mener ; Vous aimez également travailler en équipe : la bonne collaboration interne et externe est un facteur clé de réussite pour ce poste ; Vous détenez le brevet linguistique de seconde langue écrit et oral délivré par Travaillerpour.be (ancien SELOR) ou êtes en mesure de l’obtenir à terme. The Transporter Specialist for La Jornada Program focusing on transitional foster care (TFC), will be responsible for coordinating transportation and physically escorting children who have fled their country of origin and arrived in the U.S. without a parent or legal guardian as they continue their journey to be united with sponsors. Responsibilities The Transporation Specialist for La Jornada will perform duties including but not limited to: Must be able to travel out of state up to 40%-50% for reunification efforts. Performs all work in a manner consistent with the National Youth Advocate Program’s Mission, Values and Philosophies. Coordinates transportation including organizing and navigating travel destinations, physically escorts, and supervises youth while in transit to scheduled and emergency appointments. Coordinates medical transport with Charge Nurse. Coordinates clinical transport with clinical staff. Coordinates reunification transport with team. Tracks and assigns all doctor appointments via supervisors - attends weekly supervisor meeting. Maintains a daily roster of times, dates, destinations, transporters and length of transport. Provides documentation of all missed appointments or unusual events to the Management Team. Tracks and schedules all group outings weekly via transportation outing schedule. Maintains cell phone numbers of staff on transport. Ensures daily cleanliness and upkeep of all vehicles assigned to the campus – includes inspecting for cleanliness, damage, proper equipment and safe operation of vehicle. Ensures vehicles are properly fueled. Maintains security over the vehicles and keys. Reports vehicle needs and damage to maintenance and tracks all vehicle issues in regard to repair. Maintains notebooks – includes inspecting logs for completion and accuracy. Provides safety training to all new hires every three weeks. Collects and tracks all safety checklist sheets and provides weekly report. The supervision and transport of youth requires prolonged periods of walking and standing and physical agility. May be required to run and climb flights of stairs. Must be able to participate in physical interventions with youth when necessary. Must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move more than 100 pounds. Will be required to complete Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI) and CPR training. Schedule will vary depending on transport need; flexibility is needed. Other duties may be assigned Minimum Qualifications High school diploma or GED. Experience working with at-risk youth. Bilingual English/Spanish fluency is required. Excellent time management and organization skills. Excellent written and oral skills. Applicants are required to pass an agility and strength evaluation. Must have a valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, automotive insurance, and a good driving record. Proficient use of desktop and laptop computers, smartphones and tablets, printers, fax machines, and photocopiers, as well as software including word processing, spreadsheet, and database programs. Bilingual (English Spanish). Fluency in Spanish is required. Minimum automobile insurance coverage of $100,000/300,000 bodily liability coverage. 21 years of age, valid state driver’s license, reliable personal vehicle, and a good driving record. Other Skills Excellent customer service and communication skills. Sensitivity to cultural diversity. Enthusiastic self-starter. Works well independently and as a team member. The qualified candidate will follow a team concept and support agency goals, colleagues and ORR liaisons. Candidate must be able to effectively work with and be respectful and sensitive to persons from various cultures, socioeconomic, ethnic, gender, gender identity, sexual identity, disability, religious, and racial backgrounds. PHYSICAL DEMANDS Use of manual dexterity, tactile, visual, and audio acuity. Use of repetitive motion, prolonged periods of sitting and standing, and sustained visual and mental applications and demands. Occasional lifting (up to 25 pounds), bending, pulling, and carrying. Ability to travel frequently and drive vehicle while sitting for extended periods, with frequency varying based on program demands. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer who celebrates diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees by prohibiting discrimination and harassment of any kind. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Qualifications Who we are National Youth Advocate Program has been serving communities and clients since 1978 and we continue to grow each year. Our growth allows us to expand and develop new and innovative programs to meet the ever-changing needs of those we serve. We offer unique and personalized services for families and individuals in four areas: Prevention/Intervention, Positive Youth Development, Out-of-Home-Placement and Reunification/Permanency. We look for individuals that are ready to make a direct impact and are excited to be an instrument in supporting the needs of our children, youth and families.

review_candidates.title: Senior Procurement Manager
review_candidates.description: Senior Procurement Manager An infrastructure contractor running projects across western India, strengthening its central procurement Location: Remote (India) The business and the mandate This is an infrastructure contractor with projects spread across western India, from roads and bridges to utilities and industrial buildings. Spend is concentrated in cement, steel, aggregates, bitumen, equipment hire and subcontract packages, and much of it is currently decided at project level. Flexiple is a managed marketplace that helps companies hire experienced professionals, and it is finding a Senior Procurement Manager to bring this together. What would change under you Central rate contracts for steel, cement and bitumen, replacing project-by-project buying A subcontractor and equipment-hire panel with clear pre-qualification and rating Material planning linked to project schedules, so site teams are not buying on emergency Back-to-back terms with client contracts, including price variation clauses A cost-saving record that finance and the projects directors both trust How you would work You would report to the director of projects and lead a team of six, including two site-based procurement coordinators. You will negotiate with large suppliers, sit in tender reviews with the estimating team and spend one or two days a week on sites. When a price swings or a vendor slips, the call lands with you. Experience we expect Eight to twelve years in procurement, with at least four in construction, infrastructure or heavy engineering and some time leading a team. You should be comfortable with BOQs, work orders, subcontract agreements and statutory documentation. A civil engineering background or an MBA helps. The conversation path A Flexiple screening call, then a discussion with the director of projects, a case on a multi-site steel buying plan with the estimating head, a meeting with the finance director, and a final conversation with the managing director. Your single application is also weighed against other senior purchasing roles Flexiple is hiring for.
